newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat Jan car registrations hit by strikes.
newsitem.headline: Fiat Jan car registrations hit by strikes.

text.p: Registrations in January of new cars produced by Italian car group Fiat were affected by strikes which caused loss of production of around 10,000 vehicles and slowed down deliveries, an industry source said.

Fiat Auto registrations rose 1.09 percent to 93,030 units in January 1997 compared with January 1996, according to data from the Italian transport ministry. Total new car registrations in Italy were up 4.38 percent last month against January 1996.

Despite strikes by engineering and metalworkers as part of a national dispute over renewing wage contracts, the Fiat marque increased its market share in January to 36.5 from 35.1 percent previously, while new Alfa Romeo 145 and 146 models saw more than 25,000 orders from dealers in Europe, the source said.
Fiat's share of the European market remained stable at 13 percent last month, against the background of a falling market.
Positive results were seen in Germany, where the overall market was down seven percent, with Fiat models boosting their share to 5.9 percent from 5.4 percent a year previously.
